title: Static method hiding versus overriding
answer: A static method with the same signature in a subclass hides the parent method rather than overriding it. Calls are resolved using the qualifying type at compile time. If a `Parent` reference points to a `Child` object and `ref.label()` is a static call, Java chooses `Parent.label()` based on the declared reference type. This differs fundamentally from an overridden instance method, where runtime dispatch can choose the Child implementation.
